method:
One procedure, a copyist, fitted on the 192 public training pages only. It keeps the manuscript's own word stock (the 1500 commonest words of the public pages, with their frequencies), its line lengths, its page order and its paragraph marks, and writes a word at a time. For each word it does one of three things. With probability 0.30 it reaches back into what it has just written, at a distance drawn from a mixture of two exponentials (weight 0.55, tau 15 words, and weight 0.45, tau 60 words, capped at 200), and copies that word; a word fetched from within 8 words is then restated with one glyph changed with probability 0.60, while a word fetched from further back is restated that way with probability 0.50 -- a word still in the hand slips, a word fetched from a distance is written as it was. Otherwise it draws from the stock's frequency list. With probability 0.05 it invents a word, shaped by an order-3 glyph chain over the stock. Nothing else: no rule names a neighbour line, a distance, or the statistic.
FITTED, and to what. The reach mixture, the two slip rates and the 8-word split were fitted by coordinate descent to six moments measured on the public training pages: identical repeat within 200 words (0.4025), identical-or-one-glyph within 200 (0.7586), one-glyph neighbour on the line above (0.1860), the same four lines up (0.1646), within-page reuse (0.3034), and the share of identical repeats sitting within 14 words (0.2392). Two further mechanisms were tried and dropped because they did not improve that fit: a per-page lexicon (Gamma tilt on the stock) and a recency avoidance that rejects a word already written in the last 200. The repetition rate 0.30 was then set so the text reproduces the manuscript's own value of the quantity F-021 measures, and the seed was chosen as the one whose value tracks the manuscript's across 24 random 34-page subsets of the public pages (paired mean absolute deviation 0.0084; the manuscript's own spread over those subsets is 0.0078 to 0.0376, so this text is as steady as the manuscript, not steadier). The band, the null and the held-out pages were not used to choose anything; the held-out number is reported after the choice. One seed that tracked the manuscript slightly better was dropped because its text contained one four-word run of the manuscript.
WHAT CARRIES IT. Two controls, same generator, held-out pages, seeds 1 to 3. Same amount of copying but distance-blind -- reach uniform over the last 200 words: -0.008, 0.006, 0.013. No copying at all: 0.009, -0.012, 0.013. Both collapse to the chance level of sampling the manuscript's own word list (near 0.121, far 0.117, excess 0.004). So it is not repetition that produces the fact but the DISTANCE PROFILE of the repetition: short reaches slip into one-glyph variants, and that is what raises the line above the current one relative to four lines up.
RESULT. On the held-out practice pages this text gives 0.020697 against the fact's band 0.012 to 0.045, with shuffle_within_page p = 0.005 at 199 permutations: it passes. The five other seeds measured on the same held-out pages give 0.031, 0.041, 0.019, 0.043, 0.022, all passing, so the pass is not a lucky seed.
A FINDING ABOUT THE FACT ITSELF, from the public pages only: read on 34-page samples drawn from the 192 public pages, the manuscript's own value of this statistic falls below the fact's floor of 0.012 on some samples (minimum 0.0078 over 24 draws). The band is narrower than the sampling noise of the quantity it states, which is why an attack can sit inside it without resembling the manuscript in any other way, and why a failure on the hidden pages would say as much about the band as about the text.
GUARDS. 38,486 words in 4,487 ordinary lines and 738 paragraph-opening lines, exactly the manuscript's line counts; 0 four-word runs of the manuscript; 0 uncertainty markers; 5,456 distinct words, mean length 4.48.
WHAT IT WOULD SHOW, if it holds: a text with no language in it -- no morphology, no collocations, no phrase, a vocabulary sampled from a frequency list -- can carry F-021's near-versus-far elevation, because a copyist who restates what he has just written and copies what he wrote long ago produces exactly that profile. The fact would then be a statement about copying, not about meaning. WHAT IT WOULD NOT SHOW: that the manuscript was made by such a copyist, only that this fact cannot tell the two apart. ASSUMPTION THAT COULD FAIL ON THE HIDDEN PAGES: the hidden 34 pages are one draw, and on draws of that size this text's value ranges 0.011 to 0.040; a draw near either edge of the band would fail for reasons the practice pages cannot see.
